summary: Fiscal compounding boundaries use the wrong year around February
description:
Reported by Xamit Kadirbekov

Fiscal compounding boundaries use the wrong year around February

Hello Fineract developers,
 
During further review of savings arithmetic I reproduced a separate calendar correctness issue in PostingPeriod on develop e4474a0f4a4c65a75e7758e47db1fd277e5fcfef. This is distinct from FINERACT-2809 and the previously reported grace-period fraction issue.
 
Annual compounding with a March fiscal-year start chooses February 28, 2024 instead of February 29, 2024 when the period starts in March 2023. A native example with principal 1000, annual rate 36.5%, a fixed 365-day denominator, DAILY_BALANCE, and the inclusive period 2023-03-01 through 2024-02-29 returns 366.37 interest instead of 366.00. Interest compounds one day early.
 
The quarterly and biannual paths also take February's length from the business-date year and then build a date in the target year. For example, a valid one-day period on 2025-02-28 with business date 2024-06-15 and fiscal start month 3 throws DateTimeException for a fabricated February 29, 2025.
 
The public report, proposed patch, regression tests and deterministic input vectors are available here:
[https://gist.github.com/kadyrbekovhamit-cyber/e6a609ea22ed1934015e957867fd1a28]
 
The patch uses the target YearMonth and reapplies month-end adjustment after annual year rollover. Before correction, 9 of 13 focused native cases fail. After correction, those 13 cases, a further 144-case fiscal calendar corpus, and 9 existing adjacent tests pass (166 total); Spotless and Checkstyle pass on JDK 25. The additional 144-case corpus was run on the corrected version only. The tests use the real public PostingPeriod methods, Money, and dates without mocked calculations. The same PostingPeriod source is present in 1.15.0. No HTTP/account-level customer impact is claimed.
 
The closest historic report I found is FINERACT-491 / PR #423, which introduced fiscal-month support; it does not describe this leap-year mismatch. Could you point me to an existing issue, or create a separate Jira ticket so I can submit the prepared patch and tests?
 
Regards,
Xamit Kadirbekov
GERO Research

summary: Minimum dividend eligibility period is reset to the payout window
description:
Reported by Khamit

Minimum dividend eligibility period is reset to the payout window

 

Hello Fineract developers,

I reproduced the following behavior in the actual ShareProductDividendAssembler on develop e4474a0f4a4c65a75e7758e47db1fd277e5fcfef (the source is identical in tag 1.15.0):

- 100 approved shares purchased on 2026-01-01;
- product minimum active period: 90 days;
- dividend window: 2026-07-01 through 2026-08-01;
- a single active account, USD 100.00 to distribute.

The purchase age is 212 days. The assembler first clips the purchase date to July 1 and then tests 31 days against the 90-day minimum. It returns null; the production caller maps this to eligible.shares.not.found.

I interpret the documented minimum active period as eligibility age, in which case this account should qualify and receive 100.00. Please confirm whether the intended policy instead counts only days inside each payout window; that would exclude even longstanding holdings whenever the window is shorter than the configured minimum.

I prepared a patch that checks age before clipping the share-day weighting date. A 12-case native suite covers threshold equality, recent purchases and equal in-window weights for accounts with different older purchase dates. The original source fails seven cases under the holding-age interpretation. Only database read interfaces are mocked; the assembler and monetary calculations are real. No HTTP/database payout reproduction is claimed.

I found FINERACT-148/329 about dividend total rounding and FINERACT-608 about allocation; this report concerns the eligibility date instead. If the proposed interpretation is correct, could you create or identify a Jira issue for the correction?

The proposed correction passes all 12 native cases. Spotless and Checkstyle main/test checks pass.

Attachments: a detailed report with reproduction commands, a source-only patch, a patch including the native JUnit tests, and JSON test vectors.

Regards,
Khamit

summary: Prevent concurrent modification of supported cache names
description:
SpotBugs 4.9.3 reports a potential concurrency issue in
SpecifiedCacheSupportingCacheManager after the JDK upgrade from JDK 17 to JDK 25.

The supportedCacheNames field is a LinkedHashSet that can be accessed
concurrently.

setSupportedCaches() modifies the set while getCacheNames() exposes a
collection backed by the same set. Concurrent iteration and modification
can result in ConcurrentModificationException and unsafe concurrent access.

The implementation should synchronize access to supportedCacheNames and
return a snapshot from getCacheNames() so callers cannot iterate over the
internally mutable set while it is being modified.

A regression test should verify that concurrent reads and updates do not
throw an exception.
h3. Steps to reproduce
 # Create a SpecifiedCachesSupportingCacheManager instance.
 # Add initial supported cache names.
 # Start one thread repeatedly calling getCacheNames() and iterating over
 # Concurrently start another thread repeatedly calling setSupportedCaches()
 # Concurrent iteration and modification can result in ConcurrentModificationException

summary: Key Develocity CI detection to GitHub Actions
description:
settings.gradle derives {{isCI}} from the {{JENKINS_URL}} environment variable:

{code:groovy}
def isCI = System.getenv('JENKINS_URL') != null
{code}

Fineract's CI runs entirely on GitHub Actions, which never sets {{JENKINS_URL}}, and there is no Jenkins configuration anywhere in the repository. {{isCI}} is therefore always {{false}}.

Its only consumer is {{buildScan.uploadInBackground = !isCI}}, so background upload stays enabled on CI. On an ephemeral GitHub Actions runner the job can terminate before a backgrounded Build Scan upload completes, which loses the scan.

Key the check to {{GITHUB_ACTIONS}}, which GitHub Actions always sets. Uploads then happen synchronously on CI, and remain backgrounded for local developer builds where the latency matters.

summary: Expose transaction allocation history for savings account charges
description:
*As a* financial institution staff member,
*I want* to retrieve the transactions associated with an individual savings account charge, including allocated amounts and available payment references,
*so that* I can explain partial settlements, reconcile payments, and distinguish valid transactions from reversed ones.

h2. Background

A savings account charge’s balances do not provide a complete explanation of how the charge is settled. Staff need to identify the associated transactions and distinguish each transaction’s total amount from the portion allocated to the selected charge.

This distinction is particularly important for partial payments and recurring charges, where historical allocations may not correspond to the current amount due. Available payment details and receipt references help staff reconcile charge settlements with external payment records.

h2. Acceptance Criteria

* An authorized API consumer can optionally request transaction allocation history when retrieving an individual savings account charge.
* Each history entry identifies the transaction and allocation, transaction date and type, total transaction amount, amount allocated to the selected charge, and reversal status.
* Multiple partial settlements remain individually identifiable, with their respective allocated amounts.
* Reversed transactions remain visible and are explicitly marked as reversed.
* Available payment details include the payment type and receipt reference, together with any recorded account, check, routing, and bank information.
* Transactions without payment details remain visible; missing payment information does not prevent history retrieval.
* History contains only allocations for the requested charge and savings account. Transactions belonging to another account are not disclosed.
* Retrieving transaction history requires savings-account read permission in addition to the existing charge-read authorization.
* History is returned newest first, with deterministic ordering for entries on the same date.
* A charge without associated transaction allocations returns an empty history collection.
* Requests that do not ask for transaction history retain the existing response behavior.
* Retrieving history does not modify charge balances, transactions, allocations, or payment details.

h2. Notes

* The scope is the individual savings account charge read API, with history requested through {{associations=transactions}} or {{associations=all}}.
* History reflects recorded charge allocations. It does not infer payments, waivers, or write-offs from balance differences.
* Historical allocation totals must not be presented as the current outstanding balance of a recurring charge.
* Creating, collecting, waiving, reversing, or editing charges is outside this story’s scope.

Loan.repaymentScheduleInstallments is a lazy @OneToMany. Two call sites pay one extra SELECT on m_loan_repayment_schedule per loan:

1. The Loan COB readers (LoanItemReader, InlineCOBLoanItemReader) load each loan with findById, and every business step that touches the schedule then loads it separately.
2. LoanRepositoryWrapper.findByClientOfficeIdsAndLoanStatus and findByGroupOfficeIdsAndLoanStatus (used by ApplyHolidaysToLoansTasklet) list the loans and then call initializeRepaymentSchedule() on each one, which is N + 1 statements.

Proposed change: three LoanRepository queries that LEFT JOIN FETCH the schedule, used from the COB readers through a loadEntity() hook on AbstractLoanItemReader, and from LoanRepositoryWrapper in place of the per-loan initialisation loop. Only one collection is fetched per query. A second collection JOIN FETCH would be a cartesian product. WorkingCapitalInlineCOBLoanItemReader is left on findById.

Measured on a running Fineract with EclipseLink statement logging, 3 loans, Loan COB job: 3 standalone m_loan_repayment_schedule selects as-mapped, 0 with the fetch (the schedule is a LEFT OUTER JOIN on the loan query). The other lazy collections the job touches were identical in both runs.

summary: Savings hold/release transactions incorrectly affect transaction running balance
Savings amount holds can cause incorrect scheduled interest calculation
description:
h2. Description

Savings amount holds can incorrectly affect the balance used by the {*}scheduled savings interest calculation{*}.

An amount hold should reduce the available balance but should not change the account's ledger/book balance. However, the savings transaction {{runningBalance}} currently includes holds and releases.

The scheduled interest calculation operates on {{SavingsAccountData}} / {{SavingsAccountTransactionData}} DTOs and recalculates these running balances. In certain scenarios it then uses the resulting {{runningBalance}} directly as the end-of-day balance for interest calculation.

As a result, when a normal deposit or withdrawal occurs while an amount is on hold, the held amount can incorrectly affect the principal on which interest is calculated.
h2. Example

Consider the following transaction history:
{code:java}
01 Jan: Deposit       1,000
10 Jan: Hold            200
15 Jan: Withdrawal      100
20 Jan: Release         200
{code}
The correct ledger/book balances are:
{code:java}
01 Jan: 1000
10 Jan: 1000   (available balance = 800)
15 Jan:  900   (available balance = 700)
20 Jan:  900
{code}
However, the transaction running balances are recalculated approximately as:
{code:java}
Deposit       +1000   runningBalance = 1000
Amount Hold    -200   runningBalance =  800
Withdrawal     -100   runningBalance =  700
Amount Release +200   runningBalance =  900
{code}
The {{SavingsAccountTransactionData.toEndOfDayBalance()}} implementation uses {{runningBalance}} directly for ordinary withdrawals:
{code:java}
if (isWithdrawal()) {
    endOfDayBalance = Money.of(currency, this.runningBalance);
}
{code}
Therefore, after the withdrawal on 15 Jan the scheduled interest calculation can use:
{code:java}
endOfDayBalance = 700
{code}
instead of the correct ledger balance:
{code:java}
endOfDayBalance = 900
{code}
The held 200 is therefore incorrectly excluded from the balance used for interest calculation.
h2. Why the Hold Transaction Alone Does Not Expose the Problem

The hold transaction itself is not treated as a deposit or withdrawal when converting transactions to end-of-day balances. Therefore, a hold without any subsequent ledger-changing transaction may leave the interest-bearing balance unchanged.

The incorrect balance becomes observable when a later transaction, such as a withdrawal or deposit, uses the hold-adjusted {{runningBalance}} as the new end-of-day balance.

This also means that releasing the hold does not necessarily repair the interest balance, because {{AMOUNT_RELEASE}} itself is correctly not considered a ledger credit.
h2. Scheduled Interest Path

The scheduled interest job uses the DTO-based calculation path:
{code:java}
SavingsSchedularInterestPoster
 -> SavingsAccountWritePlatformService.postInterest(SavingsAccountData, ...)
 -> SavingsAccountInterestPostingServiceImpl
 -> recalculateDailyBalances(...)
 -> PostingPeriod.createFromDTO(...)
 -> SavingsAccountTransactionData.toEndOfDayBalance(...)
 -> EndOfDayBalance
 -> interest calculation
{code}
During {{{}recalculateDailyBalances(){}}}, holds and releases explicitly change the DTO running balance:
{code:java}
if (transaction.isCredit() || transaction.isAmountRelease()) {
    transactionAmount = transactionAmount.plus(transaction.getAmount());
} else if (transaction.isDebit() || transaction.isAmountOnHold()) {
    transactionAmount = transactionAmount.minus(transaction.getAmount());
}

runningBalance = runningBalance.plus(transactionAmount);
transaction.updateRunningBalance(runningBalance);
{code}
The resulting value can subsequently be used as the interest-bearing end-of-day balance.
h2. Inconsistent Behavior Between Interest Calculation Paths

The entity-based interest calculation reconstructs balances from the previous ledger balance and transaction amount.

Conceptually:
{code:java}
Deposit       -> openingBalance + amount
Hold          -> no balance change
Withdrawal    -> openingBalance - amount
Release       -> no balance change
{code}
For the example above, this produces the correct ledger balance of 900 after the withdrawal.

The DTO-based scheduled interest calculation can instead use the hold-adjusted {{runningBalance}} and produce 700.

This creates a risk that manual/entity-based interest posting and scheduled/DTO-based interest posting produce different results for the same account history.
h2. Overdraft Accounts

The DTO-based interest service also classifies transactions as positive-balance or overdraft transactions based directly on {{{}transaction.getRunningBalance(){}}}.

A hold can therefore make the derived running balance negative even while the ledger balance remains positive.

Example:
{code:java}
Ledger balance before hold:      100
Hold:                             80
Available balance:                20
Withdrawal:                       30

Ledger balance after withdrawal:  70
Available balance:               -10
Derived runningBalance:          -10
{code}
This may incorrectly classify a positive ledger balance as an overdraft balance for interest calculation.
h2. Expected Behavior

Savings interest must be calculated using the ledger/book balance. Amount holds and releases affect funds availability but must not change the balance used for interest calculation.

For the example above, interest after 15 Jan should be calculated on 900, not 700.
h2. Acceptance Criteria
 * {{AMOUNT_HOLD}} and {{AMOUNT_RELEASE}} do not affect the ledger balance used for interest calculation.
 * A withdrawal made while a hold is active is applied to the ledger balance, not to the available balance.
 * A deposit made while a hold is active is applied to the ledger balance, not to the available balance.
 * Releasing a hold does not change the interest-bearing balance.
 * Scheduled and manual interest posting produce identical results for the same transaction history.
 * Positive ledger balances are not classified as overdraft balances solely because an active hold makes the available balance negative.
 * Regression tests cover at least:
 ** deposit -> hold -> interest posting
 ** deposit -> hold -> withdrawal -> interest posting
 ** deposit -> hold -> deposit -> interest posting
 ** deposit -> hold -> withdrawal -> release -> interest posting
 ** a hold which causes available balance, but not ledger balance, to become negative
 * Tests verify both end-of-day balances and the final posted interest amount.

h2. Suggested Regression Scenario

A deterministic regression test could use:
{code:java}
Nominal annual interest rate: 36.5%
Interest calculation: daily balance
Days in year: 365
Interest posting: monthly

01 Jan: Deposit      1000
10 Jan: Hold          200
15 Jan: Withdrawal    100
20 Jan: Release       200
{code}
With a 36.5% annual rate, the daily rate is 0.1%, which makes differences in the expected interest easy to verify.

The ledger balance used for interest should be:
{code:java}
01-14 Jan: 1000, except for the exact account-activation/date semantics of the test
15 Jan onward: 900
{code}
The hold and release should not introduce an 800 or 700 ledger balance into the interest calculation.
h2. Related Issue

Related to FINERACT-2851, describing that savings {{AMOUNT_HOLD}} and {{AMOUNT_RELEASE}} transactions incorrectly affect transaction {{{}runningBalance{}}}.

summary: Enable Gradle configuration cache for local builds
description:
h2. Description

Enables the Gradle configuration cache ({{{}org.gradle.configuration-cache=true{}}}) for local builds. It had been disabled with a "temporarily disabled until we fix compatibility" note. CI keeps it off, because fresh runners using {{{}--no-daemon{}}}gain nothing from it.

Local development loops (compiling, module tests, the client modules, the quality checks, {{{}bootRun{}}}/{{{}devRun{}}}) now store the configuration cache and reuse it, including from a fresh daemon. A warm rebuild of {{:fineract-provider:compileJava}} goes from about 19s to about 1s.
h3. Build-script fixes for the configuration cache
 * {{{}static-weaving.gradle{}}}: the managed-class lookup is now a lazy provider, and the helpers moved into a plain class. The old code called {{Task.project}} and script methods from {{{}doLast{}}}.
 * {{{}fineract-provider{}}}, {{{}fineract-client{}}}, {{{}fineract-client-feign{}}}: {{{}copy{}}}/{{{}delete{}}}/{{{}fileTree{}}} in task actions now go through the injected {{{}FileSystemOperations{}}}.
 * {{fineract-doc}} {{{}doc{}}}, and {{{}checkBreakingChanges.onlyIf{}}}: values are captured at configuration time.
 * {{{}aggregateLicenseReport{}}}: the {{rename}} closure no longer captures a {{{}Project{}}}.

h3. Plugins that cannot support it are marked {{notCompatibleWithConfigurationCache}}
 * jk1 license report, jib, asciidoctor, the {{{}fineractRelease*{}}}/{{{}fineractDocPublish{}}} tasks, and the database admin tasks ({{{}createDB{}}}, {{{}createPGDB{}}}, …).
 * Builds that include these tasks fall back to running without the cache instead of failing. A full {{./gradlew build}} still includes jk1 and asciidoctor, through the binary distribution.

h3. Plugin replacements and upgrades
 * *git-versioning replaced with {{GitVersionValueSource}} (buildSrc).* The old plugin spawns git processes while the build configures. The new class ports its logic for our configuration: release/maintenance branch and tag rules, the ancestor walk and tag ordering, CI branch detection, {{-Dgit.*}} and {{VERSIONING_*}} overrides, and linked worktrees. The plugin's unused {{version}} task is gone.
 * *Spotless 6.25.0 → 8.10.2.* 6.x fails with "JVM-local cache is stale" when the cache is reused from a new daemon. The formatters are pinned to 4.29, the versions 6.25 used by default on JDK 25, so no code is reformatted. {{indentWithSpaces}} is replaced by {{{}leadingTabsToSpaces{}}}, which behaves identically.
 * *{{com.github.hierynomus.license}} (unmaintained since 2021) replaced with Spotless license headers.*
 ** Headers are still generated from {{{}APACHE_LICENSETEXT.md{}}}, for Java, XML, properties, Velocity and JSP. That's the same set of files hierynomus enforced, plus 287 files that already had correct headers.
 ** {{spotlessApply}} adds a missing header and never rewrites anything below one. A malformed header fails {{{}spotlessCheck{}}}.
 ** Also removed: the plugin's no-op {{licenseFormatMain}} wiring, and the {{spring-core:6.2.18}} buildscript pin that existed only for it.
 ** 8 Java files had a stray blank line before the header, or a malformed one. Each is fixed with a one-line deletion.
 * *jk1 dependency-license-report 2.9 → 3.1.4* (2.x is end-of-life).
 ** The bundled license texts are identical.
 ** The per-module index pages show manifest-declared licenses more cleanly; no dependency's license changes.
 ** {{generateLicenseReport}} now depends on the jars it reads, which fixes an intermittent {{ZipException: zip END header not found}} in parallel builds.

h3. CI
 * {{.github/scripts/gradle-memory-budget.sh}} writes {{{}org.gradle.configuration-cache=false{}}}.
 * The two workflows that don't use it pass {{{}--no-configuration-cache{}}}.

h3. Notes for reviewers
 * To opt out locally, pass {{{}--no-configuration-cache{}}}.
 * {{{}licenseFormat{}}}/{{{}licenseMain{}}} no longer exist. Use {{{}spotlessApply{}}}/{{{}spotlessCheck{}}} instead.
 * {{git.properties}} (actuator git info) is unaffected. It comes from gradle-git-properties.

h3. Verification
 * *Versions:* {{GitVersionValueSource}} matched the old plugin's output in 34 git scenarios, run side by side in a scratch clone. They cover develop, release/maintenance branches, tags, commits with several tags, GitHub/GitLab/Jenkins environments, overrides, worktrees, and shallow, empty and missing repositories.
 * *Outputs:* generated outputs are identical to develop: {{persistence.xml}} (15 modules), the swagger input YAML, the generated clients, and the bundled license texts.
 * *Spotless:* repo-wide {{spotlessCheck}} passes with no changes. Throwaway files confirmed that missing and malformed headers are detected and fixed, and that nothing after a header is ever changed.
 * *CI task groups, with and without the cache:* quality checks, package/war/shadowJar, unit tests, license report/CycloneDX, doc, jib ({{{}jibBuildTar{}}}), cucumber, {{{}checkBreakingChanges{}}}, and {{{}devRun{}}}/{{{}bootRun{}}} (dry run).
 * *Not tested:* sonar, pushing a jib image, tasks that need a database (integration tests, e2e cucumber, {{{}createPGDB{}}}), and the release steps.

summary: Allow to reverse Chargeback transaction
description:
The requirement is now to support *chargeback reversal* to address business use cases where a customer requests cancellation of a chargeback after it has been posted and remained effective for a certain period.
h3. 
Acceptance Criteria
 # *Undo Chargeback*

 ** The user should be able to undo a previously posted chargeback transaction on an loan account, subject to applicable business rules.

 # *Recalculate Schedule and Transactions*

 ** Upon chargeback reversal, the system should remove the chargeback impact from the loan schedule and loan calculations.

 ** The system should reverse-replay all subsequent transactions and their allocations based on the revised schedule.

 ** The resulting schedule, transaction balances, allocations, and loan calculations should reflect the state as if the chargeback had not been applied.

 ** User should be able to perform chargeback for the linked repayment again

summary: Creating or updating a report fails with 501 when a report parameter has a JSON null member
description:
h3. Steps to reproduce
On stock Fineract (develop), call {{POST /fineract-provider/api/v1/reports}} with a report parameter whose {{reportParameterName}} is an explicit JSON null, for example:

{code:json}{
  "reportName": "Null param test",
  "reportType": "Table",
  "reportCategory": "Client",
  "reportSql": "select 1",
  "reportParameters": [ { "id": "", "parameterId": 1, "reportParameterName": null } ]
}
{code}

h3. Expected
The report is created. A null {{reportParameterName}} (or a null {{id}} / {{parameterId}}) is treated the same as an absent member.

h3. Actual
The request fails with HTTP 501 Not Implemented, caused by {{java.lang.UnsupportedOperationException: JsonNull}}.

h3. Root cause
{{ReportWritePlatformServiceImpl.assembleSetOfReportParameterUsages}} guards the {{id}}, {{parameterId}} and {{reportParameterName}} members with {{JsonObject.has(name)}} only, then calls {{getAsString()}} / {{getAsLong()}}. Gson's {{has()}} returns true for a member that is present with a JSON null value, and {{getAsString()}} / {{getAsLong()}} on {{JsonNull}} throw {{UnsupportedOperationException}}, which the generic exception mapper turns into a 501. Clients that serialize unset fields as null instead of omitting them hit this on every create. The update branch has the same latent defect for {{reportParameterName}}.

h3. Proposed fix
Add {{&& !jsonObject.get(name).isJsonNull()}} next to each {{has(name)}} check in the method (id, both parameterId reads, both reportParameterName reads), so a JSON null is handled like a missing member. Unit test: a parameter with a null {{reportParameterName}} assembles without throwing.

summary: Waiving interest under creocore-strategy posts double the waived amount to the GL
description:
h3. Summary
With the {{creocore-strategy}} (and {{heavensfamily-strategy}}) repayment strategy, waiving interest on a loan records the waiver transaction's interest portion as *twice* the waived amount, so the accounting journal entries post double the waived interest.

h3. Steps to reproduce
# Create a loan product with accounting enabled (cash or accrual) and {{transactionProcessingStrategyCode}} = {{creocore-strategy}}.
# Create, approve and disburse a loan on it.
# Waive part of the interest of the first installment: {{POST /fineract-provider/api/v1/loans/{loanId}/transactions?command=waiveinterest}} with {{{"transactionDate": "<date>", "transactionAmount": 10, "locale": "en", "dateFormat": "dd MMMM yyyy"}}}
# Read the transaction back ({{GET /loans/{loanId}/transactions/{txnId}}}) and its journal entries ({{GET /journalentries?transactionId=L{txnId}}}).

h3. Expected
The waiver transaction has {{amount}} 10 and {{interestPortion}} 10, and the journal entries post one pair of 10.

h3. Actual
{{amount}} is 10 but {{interestPortion}} is 20, and the journal entries post 20 on each side. The installment's waived interest and the repayment schedule are correct; only the transaction's interest portion, and therefore the GL, is doubled.

h3. Root cause
{{LoanTransaction.updateComponents(...)}} accumulates onto the portions already set on the transaction. In {{CreocoreLoanRepaymentScheduleTransactionProcessor.handleTransactionThatIsOnTimePaymentOfInstallment}} it is called inside the {{isInterestWaiver()}} branch *and* again unconditionally after the if/else chain, so the waived interest is added twice. {{HeavensFamilyLoanRepaymentScheduleTransactionProcessor}} has the same double call in two methods ({{handleTransactionThatIsPaymentInAdvanceOfInstallment}} and {{handleTransactionThatIsOnTimePaymentOfInstallment}}; the late-payment path delegates to the latter). {{FineractStyleLoanRepaymentScheduleTransactionProcessor}} is correct: it calls {{updateComponents}} once per branch with no trailing call.

h3. Proposed fix
Remove the redundant {{updateComponents(...)}} call from the interest-waiver branch in the three methods, leaving the single trailing call. Unit tests for both processors assert that a waiver of X leaves the transaction's interest portion at X (they fail with 2X before the fix).

summary: Datatable entry with a non-numeric value for a dropdown (code lookup) column fails with HTTP 500 instead of a validation error
Audit and maker-checker search templates return empty appUsers entries
description:
h3. Steps to reproduce

On a stock Fineract instance (any tenant with at least one application user), call the audit search template:

{code}GET /fineract-provider/api/v1/audits/searchtemplate
{code}

The maker-checker search template behaves the same way:

{code}GET /fineract-provider/api/v1/makercheckers/searchtemplate
{code}

h3. Expected

Each entry of {{appUsers}} carries the user's {{id}} and {{username}}, so a UI can fill the "User" / "Checker" dropdowns of the audit and checker inbox search screens:

{code:json}{
  "appUsers": [ { "id": 1, "username": "mifos" } ],
  "actionNames": [ ... ],
  "entityNames": [ ... ],
  "statuses": [ ... ]
}
{code}

h3. Actual

HTTP 200, but every {{appUsers}} entry is an empty object. No error is logged:

{code:json}{
  "appUsers": [ {}, {} ],
  ...
}
{code}

h3. Root cause

{{AuditsApiResource.retrieveAuditSearchTemplate()}} and {{MakercheckersApiResource.retrieveAuditSearchTemplate()}} return the {{AuditSearchData}} record directly, so Jersey writes it with the Jackson object mapper ({{JerseyJacksonObjectArgumentHandler}}) instead of the Gson based {{DefaultToApiJsonSerializer}} used by the other endpoints. Jackson only picks up properties that have a getter. {{AppUserData}} has plain {{private final}} fields and no getter for {{id}} or {{username}} (Gson reads fields directly, so no other endpoint needed one), which leaves nothing for Jackson to write for each user.

h3. Proposed fix

Add Lombok {{@Getter}} to {{AppUserData.id}} and {{AppUserData.username}}, the only two fields {{AppUserData.dropdown(id, username)}} fills for the search templates. A class-level {{@Getter}} is avoided on purpose, so the other fields (roles, staff, clients, password flags) are not exposed through this Jackson path. The Gson based endpoints that use {{AppUserData}} are unaffected.

h3. Test

A serialization test that writes an {{AuditSearchData}} with the Jersey {{objectMapper}} bean and asserts each {{appUsers}} entry contains exactly {{id}} and {{username}}. It fails on current {{develop}} (empty objects) and passes with the fix.

summary: Reading a group's calendars fails with HTTP 500 when it has a non-repeating calendar
description:
h3. Summary

Reading calendars fails with a {{NullPointerException}} as soon as the entity has a *non-repeating* calendar. A non-repeating calendar is stored with {{recurrence = NULL}} (by design, see {{Calendar}} constructor and {{Calendar.update}}), but the row mappers in {{CalendarReadPlatformServiceImpl}} pass that null rule straight into {{CalendarUtils}}, which hands it to ical4j's {{RRule}} parser.

h3. Steps to reproduce (stock Fineract)
# Create a group: {{POST /v1/groups}} (any office, active).
# Add a non-repeating, non-collection calendar to it:

{code:json}POST /v1/groups/{groupId}/calendars
{ "title": "One-off meeting", "typeId": 4, "repeating": false, "startDate": "28 September 2026", "locale": "en", "dateFormat": "dd MMMM yyyy" }
{code}
# Read it back: {{GET /v1/groups/{groupId}/calendars/{calendarId}}}, or list {{GET /v1/groups/{groupId}/calendars}}. The same mapper also backs other calendar reads, e.g. {{GET /v1/loans/template?templateType=jlgbulk&groupId={groupId}}}.

h3. Expected

HTTP 200. The calendar is returned with {{repeating: false}}, no {{frequency}} / {{repeatsOnDay}} / {{repeatsOnNthDayOfMonth}} and {{interval: 0}}, the same defaults already used for a rule that cannot be parsed.

h3. Actual

The request fails with HTTP 500 ({{Internal Server Error}}); the server log shows a {{NullPointerException}} ({{Cannot invoke "String.split(String)" because "aValue" is null}}) thrown from {{CalendarUtils.getICalRecur}} (ical4j {{RRule}} with a null rule string), reached from {{CalendarReadPlatformServiceImpl$CalendarDataMapper.mapRow}}.

h3. Root cause

Both {{CalendarDataMapper}} and {{CalendarDataFromHistoryMapper}} call {{CalendarUtils.getFrequency}}, {{getInterval}}, {{getRepeatsOnDay}}, {{getRepeatsOnNthDayOfMonth}} and {{getMonthOnDay}} unconditionally. Each of them parses the rule with {{getICalRecur(recurrence)}}, which cannot handle {{null}}. The neighbouring {{humanReadable}} computation in the same mappers already guards with {{recurrence != null}}; the other five calls do not.

h3. Proposed fix

Guard those five calls with {{recurrence != null}} in both mappers and fall back to {{CalendarFrequencyType.INVALID}}, {{0}}, {{CalendarWeekDaysType.INVALID}}, {{NthDayType.INVALID}} and {{null}} (which {{CalendarEnumerations}} already renders as "no value"). Repeating calendars are unaffected.

h3. Test

A unit test {{CalendarReadPlatformServiceImplTest}} maps a non-repeating calendar row (null recurrence) through {{retrieveCalendar}} and checks the defaults, plus a repeating row to show the rule is still parsed.

summary: A renamed report, or one whose permission was granted to a role, cannot be deleted
description:
h3. Summary

Creating a report ({{POST /reports}}) also creates its {{READ_<reportName>}} permission, and deleting it ({{DELETE /reports/{id}}}) looks that permission up by the report's _current_ name and deletes it. Two defects in {{ReportWritePlatformServiceImpl}} make a user-created report impossible to delete:
# *Renaming a report does not rename its permission.* {{updateReport}} changes {{reportName}} but never touches the companion {{m_permission}} row, so the permission keeps the old {{READ_<oldName>}} code. Users/roles then see and grant a permission named after a report that no longer exists, and {{deleteReport}} later fails with {{PermissionNotFoundException: Permission with Code READ_<newName> does not exist}} — the report can never be deleted.
# *Deleting a report whose READ permission was granted to a role fails.* {{deleteReport}} calls {{permissionRepository.delete(permission)}} directly. {{m_role_permission}} is maintained only from the owning {{Role}} side of the {{@ManyToMany}}, so the join rows are not removed and the delete violates the {{m_role_permission}} → {{m_permission}} foreign key.

h3. Steps to reproduce

Rename case:
# {{POST /fineract-provider/api/v1/reports}}
   {code:json}   {"reportName": "Rename test", "reportType": "Table", "reportCategory": "Client", "reportSql": "select 1", "useReport": true}
   {code}
# {{PUT /fineract-provider/api/v1/reports/{id}}} with {{{"reportName": "Rename test 2"}}} → 200.
# {{GET /fineract-provider/api/v1/permissions}} still lists {{READ_Rename test}}, and no {{READ_Rename test 2}}.
# {{DELETE /fineract-provider/api/v1/reports/{id}}} → *404* {{error.msg.resource.not.found}} / {{error.msg.permission.code.invalid}}: "Permission with Code READ\_Rename test 2 does not exist". The report stays and can never be deleted through the API.

Role grant case:
# Create a report as above (name {{Grant test}}).
# {{PUT /fineract-provider/api/v1/roles/{roleId}/permissions}} with {{{"permissions": {"READ_Grant test": true}}}}.
# {{DELETE /fineract-provider/api/v1/reports/{id}}} → *403* {{error.msg.data.integrity.issue}}: {{update or delete on table "m_permission" violates foreign key constraint "fk8dedb048103b544b" on table "m_role_permission"}}. The transaction rolls back and the report stays.

h3. Expected

Renaming a report renames its {{READ_}} permission; deleting a report removes the report and its permission, including any role grants of it.

h3. Actual

Reproduced on current {{develop}}: 404 in the rename case, 403 (data integrity) in the role-grant case; the report cannot be deleted in either case.

h3. Proposed fix
* {{Permission.updateEntityName(String)}} recomputes {{entityName}} and {{code}}; {{updateReport}} looks up {{READ_<previousName>}} when {{reportName}} changes and renames it.
* {{deleteReport}} tolerates a missing permission (logs a warning and deletes the report), so reports already renamed before the fix can still be deleted.
* {{RoleRepository.findByPermissionId(Long)}}; {{deleteReport}} removes the permission from every role holding it before deleting the permission.

A unit test ({{ReportWritePlatformServiceImplPermissionTest}}) covers rename, update without rename, delete with no permission, and delete with a role grant.

summary: Duplicate product name / account number returns "Unknown data integrity issue" on PostgreSQL instead of the "already exists" error
description:
h3. Summary

On PostgreSQL, creating a savings product, fixed deposit product, loan product, savings/deposit account or loan whose unique field (name, short name, external ID, account number) is already taken does not return the specific "already exists" error. The request fails with the generic "Unknown data integrity issue" message instead, so the user cannot tell which field is the problem.

h3. Steps to reproduce (stock Fineract on PostgreSQL)
# {{POST /fineract-provider/api/v1/savingsproducts}} with a valid body, e.g.

{code:json}{"name":"Dup SP","shortName":"DSP","currencyCode":"USD","digitsAfterDecimal":2,"inMultiplesOf":0,"nominalAnnualInterestRate":0,"interestCompoundingPeriodType":1,"interestPostingPeriodType":4,"interestCalculationType":1,"interestCalculationDaysInYearType":365,"accountingRule":1,"locale":"en"}
{code}
# Send the same request again (or the same name with a different short name).
# Likewise {{POST /v1/loanproducts}} with the name of an existing loan product.

h3. Expected

{{error.msg.savingsproduct.duplicate.name}} ("Savings product with name {{Dup SP}} already exists", parameter {{name}}), and {{error.msg.product.loan.duplicate.name}} for the loan product.

h3. Actual

Both the second savings product request and the loan product request answer HTTP 403 with the generic fallback:

{code:json}{"httpStatusCode":"403","defaultUserMessage":"Unknown data integrity issue with savings product.","userMessageGlobalisationCode":"error.msg.savingsproduct.unknown.data.integrity.issue"}
{code}

{code:json}{"httpStatusCode":"403","defaultUserMessage":"Unknown data integrity issue with resource.","userMessageGlobalisationCode":"error.msg.product.loan.unknown.data.integrity.issue"}
{code}

The same happens for a duplicate account number or external ID on savings/deposit accounts and loans.

h3. Root cause

The {{handleDataIntegrityIssues}} methods match the violated constraint by name, using the explicit names from the old MySQL schema ({{sp_unq_name}}, {{sp_unq_short_name}}, {{sa_account_no_UNIQUE}}, {{sa_external_id_UNIQUE}} / {{sa_externalid_UNIQUE}}, {{unq_name}}, {{external_id}}, {{loan_account_no_UNIQUE}}, {{loan_externalid_UNIQUE}}). The Liquibase changelog declares these columns with a plain {{unique="true"}} and no constraint name, so on PostgreSQL the constraints get PostgreSQL's generated names:

||table||constraints on PostgreSQL||
|{{m_savings_product}}|{{m_savings_product_name_key}}, {{m_savings_product_short_name_key}}|
|{{m_savings_account}}|{{m_savings_account_account_no_key}}, {{m_savings_account_external_id_key}}|
|{{m_product_loan}}|{{m_product_loan_name_key}}, {{m_product_loan_external_id_key}}, {{m_product_loan_short_name_key}}|
|{{m_loan}}|{{m_loan_account_no_key}}, {{m_loan_external_id_key}}|

None of the handlers' strings occur in PostgreSQL's {{duplicate key value violates unique constraint "..."}} message, so every branch is skipped and the generic fallback is thrown. {{LoanProductWritePlatformServiceJpaRepositoryImpl}} already works around this for the short name only ({{containsDuplicateShortnameErrorForPostgreSQL}}, matching {{m_product_loan_short_name_key}}); name and external ID never got the same treatment.

h3. Proposed fix

In each handler, also match the PostgreSQL-generated constraint name next to the existing one, without changing the error codes or messages:
* {{SavingsProductWritePlatformServiceJpaRepositoryImpl}}, {{FixedDepositProductWritePlatformServiceJpaRepositoryImpl}} (same {{m_savings_product}} table)
* {{SavingsApplicationProcessWritePlatformServiceJpaRepositoryImpl}}, {{DepositApplicationProcessWritePlatformServiceJpaRepositoryImpl}}
* {{LoanProductWritePlatformServiceJpaRepositoryImpl}} (name, external ID)
* {{LoanApplicationWritePlatformServiceJpaRepositoryImpl}} (account number, external ID)

Renaming the constraints in a migration would also work but touches existing databases; the matching change is local and keeps MySQL/MariaDB behaviour as it is.

h3. Test

A unit test for {{SavingsProductWritePlatformServiceJpaRepositoryImpl}} that feeds a PostgreSQL unique-violation ({{m_savings_product_name_key}} / {{m_savings_product_short_name_key}}) through {{create}} and asserts the {{duplicate.name}} / {{duplicate.short.name}} codes, plus the existing MySQL-name case.

summary: Post Interest For Savings job stops posting interest on idle savings accounts after the first posting (pivot-date mode)
description:
h3. Summary

When the global configuration {{allow-backdated-transaction-before-interest-posting}} is *disabled* (pivot-date mode), the _Post Interest For Savings_ job posts interest on a savings account only once. Every later run silently posts nothing for that account for as long as it has no new deposit or withdrawal, however many posting periods have passed: the job succeeds, no interest transaction is created and {{interestPostedTillDate}} does not move.

h3. Steps to reproduce (stock Fineract, {{develop}})
# Enable {{enable-business-date}} and *disable* {{allow-backdated-transaction-before-interest-posting}} ({{PUT /v1/configurations/{id}}} with {{{"enabled": false}}}).
# Set the business date (and COB date) to {{2026-08-15}}.
# Savings product: 5% nominal annual interest, daily compounding, monthly posting, daily balance, 365 days, no accounting.
# Create, approve and activate a savings account on {{2026-06-01}} and deposit {{1000}} on {{2026-06-01}}.
# Run the job: {{POST /v1/jobs/short-name/SA_PINT?command=executeJob}}. Interest is posted for June and July (transactions on {{2026-07-01}} and {{2026-08-01}}), {{interestPostedTillDate}} becomes {{2026-08-01}}.
# Without any other activity on the account, move the business date (and COB date) to {{2026-10-15}} and run the job again.

h3. Expected

Interest is posted for August and September (transactions on {{2026-09-01}} and {{2026-10-01}}) on the carried-forward balance, and {{interestPostedTillDate}} advances.

h3. Actual

The second run posts nothing: no new interest transaction, {{interestPostedTillDate}} stays at {{2026-08-01}}, no error. The account never earns interest again until a new deposit or withdrawal is made.

h3. Root cause

In pivot-date mode {{SavingsAccountReadPlatformServiceImpl#retrieveAllSavingsDataForInterestPosting}} only loads the transactions dated on or after {{interest_posted_till_date}}, and the earlier history is carried in as {{runningBalanceOnPivotDate}}, which {{SavingsAccountInterestPostingServiceImpl#calculateInterestUsing}} uses as the starting balance of the first period. For an account with no activity since the last posting, the non-interest-posting transaction list is therefore empty.

{{SavingsAccountInterestPostingServiceImpl#appendPostingPeriodIfAny}} returns early when its transaction list is empty, without creating a {{PostingPeriod}}. The carried-forward balance never earns interest, although {{PostingPeriod#createFromDTO}} already handles an empty list: it builds one end-of-day balance at the opening balance spanning the whole period. The first posting is not affected only because {{interest_posted_till_date}} is still null then, so the full history is loaded.

h3. Proposed fix

In {{appendPostingPeriodIfAny}}, skip a period without transactions only when the balance carried into it is also zero; otherwise create the {{PostingPeriod}} with the empty list and let its flat-balance fallback compute the interest. The overdraft split calls (primary/secondary lists filtered per month) keep the current early return, because there an empty list means "this side does not apply in the period" and building a period from the carried balance would count interest twice.

h3. Test

A unit test for {{SavingsAccountInterestPostingServiceImpl#calculateInterestUsing}}: an account in pivot-date mode with no transactions after the pivot date and a non-zero {{runningBalanceOnPivotDate}} must get one posting period per elapsed posting period with non-zero interest; with a zero carried balance no period is produced.

summary: Entity Data Table Checks – Newly created data table (Loan Product / m_product_loan) does not appear in the Data Table dropdown
description:
Summary
A new data table was created in Admin > System > Manage Data Tables for the Loan Product entity (m_product_loan) and saved successfully. It doesn't appear in the Data Table dropdown when creating an Entity Data Table Check for Entity = Loan Product. The dropdown is empty, so the check can't be created.

Environment
CBS Portal DEV (lms-core-banking-portal-dev.foo-apps.com)

Logged in as Admin

Steps to Reproduce
Go to Admin > System > Manage Data Tables and click Create Data Table.

Enter Data Table Name test, choose Entity Type Loan Product, and leave Multi Row unchecked.

Click Add Columns, add column name (Type String, Length 30), then click Submit.

The data table test is created (Associated With: m_product_loan) and shows in the Manage Data Tables list.

Go to Admin > Organization > Entity Data Table Checks and click Create.

Choose Entity Loan Product and Status CREATE.

Open the Data Table dropdown.

Actual Result
The Data Table dropdown has no options. The newly created table test isn't listed.

The field shows the validation message "Data Table is required", and Submit stays disabled.

The user can't create an entity data table check for the new Loan Product data table.

Expected Result
The Data Table dropdown lists every registered data table associated with the selected entity. For Entity = Loan Product, that includes test (m_product_loan).

The user can choose it, pick a status, and submit the Entity Data Table Check.

summary: Editing a Template fails
description:
Summary:
When attempting to edit an existing template ("Loan Agreement Template"), submitting the edit fails and an untranslated backend error key is displayed instead of the change being saved. The error message text ("id.not-null") suggests the template ID is not being sent/recognized on update, blocking the edit entirely.

Steps to Reproduce:

Navigate to Templates > Loan Agreement Template.

Click Edit (URL: /#/templates/34/edit).

Modify the template Name and/or Text fields.

Click "Submit".

Expected Result:
The template updates successfully and the user is returned to the template view (or a confirmation is shown), with the edited content saved.

Actual Result:
An error banner appears: {org.apache.fineract.infrastructure.template.id.not-null} — a raw, untranslated backend error key rather than a user-friendly message. The edit does not save, and the user cannot proceed.

Loan Accounts - Incorrect duplicate guarantor validation message and added guarantors are not displayed
description:
Multiple issues occur when managing guarantors for a Loan Account.

Scenario 1 — Incorrect duplicate guarantor validation message
When attempting to add a client who already exists as a guarantor for the same loan, the system correctly prevents the duplicate guarantor from being added. However, the displayed validation message is grammatically incorrect.

Current message:

X is already exist as a guarantor for this loan

The message should be updated to provide a clear and grammatically correct user-facing validation message.

Scenario 2 — Added guarantors are not displayed in View Guarantors
A loan can have multiple guarantors successfully added to it. However, when navigating to View Guarantors, the Guarantors Details table is empty and none of the previously added guarantors are displayed.

This prevents users from reviewing existing guarantors associated with the loan and makes it unclear whether the guarantors were successfully stored.

Steps to Reproduce
Scenario 1 — Duplicate guarantor validation
Navigate to Clients.

Open a client with an existing Loan Account.

Open the relevant Loan Account.

Navigate to the guarantor management section.

Add an existing client as a guarantor and submit successfully.

Attempt to add the same client again as a guarantor for the same loan.

Observe the displayed validation message.

Actual Result
The system displays:

X is already exist as a guarantor for this loan

Expected Result
The system should display:

X already exists as a guarantor for this loan

where X represents the guarantor's name.

Scenario 2 — View Guarantors does not display existing guarantors
Navigate to Clients.

Open a client with a Loan Account.

Add one or more guarantors to the Loan Account.

Confirm that the guarantor creation actions are completed successfully.

Navigate to View Guarantors.

Observe the Guarantors Details table.

Actual Result
The Guarantors Details table is empty and no guarantors are displayed, even though multiple guarantors have already been added to the Loan Account.

Expected Result
All existing guarantors associated with the Loan Account should be displayed in the Guarantors Details table with their corresponding information, including where applicable:

Name

Relationship

Guarantor Type

Deposit Account

Amount

Remaining Amount

Status

Available actions

summary: Account Transfer: "Undo Account Transfer" fails with "Insufficient spendable balance" error — user cannot reverse a completed savings-to-savings transfer
description:
Screen
Clients > Nour Hashem Ismail > Savings > Account Transfers > 1617 (View Account Transfer)

Test Data
Transfer ID: 1617
Amount: AED 4.00
Transaction Date / Value Date: 24 September 2026
From: Savings Account 000000899 (IBAN LB05099900080000000000000899), client Nour Hashem Ismail, Axian Main Office
To: Savings Account SVAE000000386 (IBAN LB790999000800SVAE000000386), client Nour Hashem Ismail, Axian Main Office

Preconditions

An account transfer of AED 4.00 has been successfully posted from savings account 000000899 to savings account SVAE000000386.

The transferred amount is still sitting in the destination account (SVAE000000386).

Steps to Reproduce

Log in to the CBS Portal as Admin.

Navigate to Clients > Nour Hashem Ismail > Savings account 000000899 > Account Transfers.

Open account transfer 1617.

Click "Undo Account Transfer".

Expected Result
The transfer is reversed: AED 4.00 is debited back from the destination account SVAE000000386 and credited to the source account 000000899, both original transactions are marked as reversed, the corresponding GL entries are reversed, and a success message is shown.

Actual Result
The undo is rejected and the following error toast is displayed:
"Insufficient spendable balance: Requested amount 4.000000 exceeds spendable balance 0.00 (Available: 0.00, Overdraft: 0) as of value date 2026-09-24"
The transfer remains in place and there is no way for the user to reverse it from the portal.

Impact
Operators cannot correct erroneous or duplicate transfers through the standard Undo action, forcing manual journal entries or back-office workarounds and leaving the customer's balances incorrect.

Suspected Root Cause
The spendable-balance validation on savings debits appears to be applied to the undo/reversal flow. Either (a) the check is evaluated against the wrong account (the source account 000000899, whose spendable balance is 0.00 after the transfer, instead of the destination account SVAE000000386 that is actually being debited), or (b) the reversal of the credit leg is treated as a fresh withdrawal and subjected to the same spendable-balance rule as a new customer debit. An undo of a transfer should only need the destination account to hold the originally credited amount; the source account's balance should not block it.

summary: Savings overdraft interest split ignores transactions after the first month of a quarterly,   bi-annual or annual posting period
description:
h3. Environment / configuration

  * Savings product with *Allow overdraft* enabled (overdraft limit and overdraft interest      rate set)
  * Accounting: *Accrual (periodic)*, with an *interest receivable* GL account mapped
  * Nominal annual interest rate: 10%
  * Interest compounding period: Daily
  * Interest posting period: *Quarterly*
  * Interest calculated using: Daily balance
  * Days in year: 365
  * Global configuration \{{enable-business-date}} enabled
  * Global configuration \{{allow-backdated-transaction-before-interest-posting}}: default (enabled)

  h3. Steps to reproduce

  # Create a client and a savings account on the product above.
  # Approve and activate the account on 2025-01-01.
  # Deposit 10,000 on 2025-01-01.
  # Deposit 10,000 on 2025-02-15.
  # Set the business date to 2025-04-02.
  # Run the *Post Interest For Savings* job.
  # Check the interest posted for the Q1 period (2025-01-01 to 2025-03-31).

  h3. Expected result

  Q1 interest covers both balances:
  * 10,000 from 2025-01-01 to 2025-02-14 (45 days)
  * 20,000 from 2025-02-15 to 2025-03-31 (45 days)

  Q1 interest: *373.64*

  h3. Actual result

  Q1 interest: *124.03*

  This is the interest on the first 10,000 for 2025-01-01 to 2025-02-14 only. The 2025-02-15 deposit and the
  balance
  from 2025-02-15 to 2025-03-31 are not included. Shortfall: *249.61* (about two-thirds of the expected
  interest).

  h3. Differential

  The overdraft/interest-receivable split applies only when the account allows overdraft *and* has an
  interest
  receivable GL account. With the same inputs but without overdraft/interest receivable (non-split branch of
  \{{SavingsAccountInterestPostingServiceImpl#calculateInterestUsing}}), Q1 interest is *373.64*, the
  expected value.

  Both figures were reproduced with a unit test calling
  \{{SavingsAccountInterestPostingServiceImpl#calculateInterestUsing}}
  with the configuration above (up-to date 2025-04-02, MathContext precision 10, HALF_EVEN).

  h3. Root cause

  {{fineract-savings/src/main/java/org/apache/fineract/portfolio/savings/service/SavingsAccountInterestPosti
  ngServiceImpl.java}},
  lines 362-406, introduced in FINERACT-2312 (commit a6fa1adc99).

  \{{listForOverdraft}}, \{{listForInterestPosting}} and \{{isOverdraftAccount}} select transactions for a
  posting
  period by comparing only the calendar month:

  \{code:java}
  periodInterval.startDate().getMonth() == tx.getDate().getMonth()
  \{code}

  This ignores the year and the posting period's actual start and end dates. For a quarterly period starting
  in
  January, only January transactions are selected. Transactions dated in February or March are excluded, and
  because each transaction's balance ends the day before the next transaction, the days after the last
  selected
  transaction carry no balance in the posting period.

  The same applies to bi-annual and annual posting periods.

  h3. Second symptom (same root cause, NOT reproduced)

  The same month-equality comparison also ignores the year. When account history spans multiple years
  (e.g. with \{{allow-backdated-transaction-before-interest-posting}} enabled, where the full transaction
  history is
  loaded), transactions from the same calendar month of an earlier year are included in the current period's
  lists and in the overdraft/non-overdraft classification made by \{{isOverdraftAccount}}. This can
  misclassify a
  period as overdraft or non-overdraft; a possible consequence is interest being posted with the wrong type
  or
  counted twice for the same interval. This has not been reproduced.

summary: DataValidatorBuilder.validateForBooleanValue() throws NullPointerException when value is null and ignoreIfNull() is not set
description:
DataValidatorBuilder.validateForBooleanValue() delegates to the private validateStringFor(...). That method only returns early for a null value when ignoreIfNull() was called. Otherwise it goes on to call this.value.toString() and throws a NullPointerException. The class's value-format checks (e.g. validateCronExpression, inMinMaxRange, positiveAmount) skip null and leave missing-value reporting to notNull()/notBlank().

Observed in a unit test on develop (386ee1523f):

java.lang.NullPointerException: Cannot invoke "Object.toString()" because "this.value" is null
    at org.apache.fineract.infrastructure.core.data.DataValidatorBuilder.validateStringFor(DataValidatorBuilder.java:962)
    at org.apache.fineract.infrastructure.core.data.DataValidatorBuilder.validateForBooleanValue(DataValidatorBuilder.java:978)

Affected callers

Jobs (reproduced on a running server). Against a locally running Fineract instance (devRun, pre-fix build), PUT /v1/jobs/{jobId}:

- {"active": null} returns HTTP 500 Internal Server Error (observed).
- {"active": ""} returns HTTP 500 Internal Server Error (observed).

JobDetailDataValidator reads the value with extractStringNamed(), which returns null for both inputs. It then calls .notBlank().validateForBooleanValue(): notBlank() records the "cannot.be.blank" error, and the NPE is thrown before that error can be returned as an HTTP 400.

Code values and entity datatable checks (from reading the code, not reproduced against a running server). An explicit JSON null makes the extractor return null, and the validator then throws.

- Code value create/update with {"isActive": null} (CodeValueCommandFromApiJsonDeserializer).
- Entity datatable check create with {"systemDefined": null} (EntityDatatableChecksDataValidator).

Relation to FINERACT-1013

FINERACT-1013 (closed as "Not A Problem", Dec 2025) was also about validateForBooleanValue(). It was closed because extractBooleanNamed() pre-parses the value via Boolean.parseBoolean(), so invalid strings never reach the method. That reasoning doesn't hold here, for three reasons:

- It only covers non-null strings. An explicit JSON null is a JsonNull, not a JsonPrimitive, so extractBooleanNamed() returns null without parsing anything. The null reaches validateForBooleanValue() and fails at this.value.toString().
- Two of the three callers don't use extractBooleanNamed() at all. JobDetailDataValidator and EntityDatatableChecksDataValidator use extractStringNamed(), so nothing pre-parses the value. A non-boolean value such as "yes" reaches the method and is rejected with value.should.true.or.false. The method is not dead code on these paths. A new unit test confirms the method rejects "yes"; that the value arrives there unparsed comes from reading the code.
- Empty strings take the same route. extractStringNamed() also returns null for "" and whitespace-only values. This is observed on the jobs path: PUT /v1/jobs/{jobId} with {"active": ""} returned HTTP 500 on a running pre-fix instance.

Expected

A null value is skipped by validateForBooleanValue(), the same way the other value-format checks handle null, so callers get their normal validation errors (HTTP 400) instead of an NPE.

Related issues

Relates to FINERACT-2694: same defect family (a queued DataValidatorBuilder validation error is bypassed by a null dereference, giving a 500 instead of a 400), but a different call path (.intValue()/fromInt(), not validateForBooleanValue()).

summary: Create Accounting Rules with list of accounts
description:
Summary
Creating or updating an Accounting Rule using tag-based debit/credit accounts (creditTags / debitTags) always fails with a 400 Bad Request validation error, even when the request payload is valid and contains existing tag IDs retrieved from GET /v1/accountingrules/template.

The issue affects both create and update Accounting Rule APIs because the tag-based fields are removed during request binding before validation is performed.

Steps to Reproduce
Call:



GET /v1/accountingrules/template
Retrieve valid IDs from:

allowedCreditTagOptions

allowedDebitTagOptions

Example:

22 → Cash

23 → Bank

Create an Accounting Rule using tags:



{
  "name": "Compound Cash-Bank Rule",
  "officeId": 1,
  "creditTags": [22, 23],
  "debitTags": [24, 205],
  "allowMultipleCreditEntries": true,
  "allowMultipleDebitEntries": true,
  "description": "test compound rule"
}
Actual Result
The API returns:



400 Bad Request
with validation errors:



"The parameter accountToCredit or creditTags required"
"The parameter accountToDebit or debitTags required"
Server-side request logging confirms that the incoming JSON payload contains creditTags and debitTags correctly. However, these fields are missing before validation is executed.

Expected Result
The Accounting Rule should be created or updated successfully using the provided debit and credit tags, in the same way that rules using accountToDebit and accountToCredit currently work.

Root Cause
The issue is caused by AccountRuleRequest:



fineract-accounting/src/main/java/org/apache/fineract/accounting/rule/data/request/AccountRuleRequest.java
This class is the request DTO used by JAX-RS to bind the request body in:

AccountingRuleApiResource#createAccountingRule

AccountingRuleApiResource#updateAccountingRule

The DTO only contains:

name

officeId

accountToDebit

accountToCredit

description

but does not define:

creditTags

debitTags

allowMultipleCreditEntries

allowMultipleDebitEntries

During request processing, the bound AccountRuleRequest object is re-serialized:



apiJsonSerializerService.serialize(accountRuleRequest)
and the generated JSON is passed to:



AccountingRuleCommandFromApiJsonDeserializer
for validation.

Since the missing fields are not part of the DTO, they are discarded during deserialization and never appear in the serialized command JSON. As a result, validation always receives null values for creditTags and debitTags, causing the request to fail even though the client sent valid data.

Impact
Tag-based Accounting Rules cannot currently be created or updated through the REST API.

Verification on the development tenant showed that all existing Accounting Rules use:

accountToDebit

accountToCredit

and no rules currently use creditTags or debitTags, confirming that tag-based rules have not been functional through the API.

Required Fix
Update AccountRuleRequest to support all Accounting Rule fields, including:

creditTags

debitTags

allowMultipleCreditEntries

allowMultipleDebitEntries

Ensure these fields are preserved during request binding and re-serialization so that AccountingRuleCommandFromApiJsonDeserializer can validate and process tag-based Accounting Rules correctly.

description:
When user clicks on settle receivable, all charges should be settled 


Summary
Clicking Settle Receivables on a Hold and Post account has no effect. The account has two Active receivable holds that are fully funded by the ledger balance, but after confirming the action both holds stay Active, no Pay Charge transaction is posted, and the balances do not change.

Per the ticket description: "When user clicks on settle receivable, all charges should be settled."

Starting State (Holds Details tab)
Account Overview: Ledger Balance = AED 3.00, Available Balance = AED 0.00, Total Held Amount = AED 3.00

Hold ID

Created

Status

Hold Type

Linked Charge

Initial Amount

Remaining Amount

1025189

02/10/2026

Active

Receivable

7211 - Weekly charge

2.00

2.00

1025185

02/10/2026

Released (struck through)

Receivable

7211 - Weekly charge

4.00

0.00

1025183

02/10/2026

Active

Receivable

7211 - Weekly charge

1.00

1.00

The two Active holds total AED 3.00, which exactly matches both the Total Held Amount and the Ledger Balance. The funds are already reserved and fully cover the held amount, so nothing should block settlement.

Steps to Reproduce
Open account 000010845 → Holds Details tab and confirm the starting state above.

Open the account action menu (☰) → Settle Receivables.

In the "Are you sure you want to settle receivables?" dialog, click Confirm.

The page reloads (URL gets ?_r=…). Review the Holds Details tab and Account Overview.

Actual Result
The screen after confirming is identical to the screen before:

Holds 1025189 (2.00) and 1025183 (1.00) are both still Active, with their full Remaining Amount unchanged.

Ledger Balance is still AED 3.00, Available Balance is still AED 0.00, and Total Held Amount is still AED 3.00.

There is no error message and no visible confirmation.

Expected Result
Both Active holds should be Posted, with Remaining Amount = 0.00.

AED 3.00 should be posted against charge 7211 (Weekly charge) as Pay Charge transaction(s), and the charge's Paid/Outstanding figures should update to match.

The account should end with Ledger Balance AED 0.00, Total Held Amount AED 0.00, and Available Balance AED 0.00.

Suspected Area
Silent no-op. The action completes without an error but changes nothing. It's worth checking whether the Settle Receivables endpoint actually selects these hold records, for example whether its query filters them out by status, due date, or charge state, and whether it returns success without processing anything.

Partial holds against one charge. All three holds belong to the same charge (7211). One was released, and two small partial holds (2.00 and 1.00) are still active. If settlement only runs when the held amount covers the charge's full outstanding amount, then partial holds like these would never be posted. That would contradict the requirement that all held charges get settled.

summary: Allow an optional transactionDate when waiving a loan charge
description:
Waiving a loan charge offers no way to choose the waiver's transaction date. {{LoanChargeWritePlatformServiceImpl}} derives it: the charge's due date if that has passed, otherwise the current business date. That date also drives schedule recalculation and the loan's lifecycle transition, so a waiver that closes a loan stamps the closing date as well.

When a waiver is the consequence of an earlier-dated event, it gets the date the request happened to be processed, not the date of the event. An example is a backdated repayment that settles the loan. Statements, the closing date and any later replay then follow the processing date. Correcting the date after the fact is not safe, because the recalculation and the lifecycle transition have already used it.

*Proposed change:*
 * Accept an optional {{transactionDate}} (with {{{}dateFormat{}}}/{{{}locale{}}}) on the waive-charge command.

 * When it is given, use it in place of the derived date for the waiver transaction, for the schedule recalculation and for the lifecycle transition.

 * Validate it as other loan transaction dates are validated: not in the future, not before disbursement.

 * When it is absent, behaviour is unchanged.

 * Add unit and integration tests for a backdated waiver that closes the loan.

summary: Allow subclasses to customise payment allocation in AdvancedPaymentScheduleTransactionProcessor
description:
Customising how a payment is distributed across allocation buckets currently means copying AdvancedPaymentScheduleTransactionProcessor whole. An example is limiting how much of an in-advance payment a given charge may absorb.

processPaymentAllocation is private and reached from many places inside the class. Several core classes check instanceof AdvancedPaymentScheduleTransactionProcessor, so a replacement must also extend it. A subclass cannot redirect those calls, so an extension ends up as a full copy that has to be kept in step with every release.

*Proposed change:*
 * Make processPaymentAllocation protected, or extract a protected hook for the per-bucket amount, called where the amount for a bucket is decided.

 * Default behaviour is unchanged.

summary: Charges submitted on the same day replay in creation order instead of due-date order
description:
On progressive loans, ChangeOperation#compareTo orders charges by effective date, then by submitted date, then by creation time. Two charges submitted on the same day therefore replay in creation order.

When a payment made before that day is reprocessed, it is applied to those charges in that order. A charge due later can then be paid ahead of one due earlier. The order of rows in the loan's charge set is not meaningful, so the outcome can differ between otherwise identical loans.

*Steps to reproduce:*

# Create a progressive loan.
# Add several specified-due-date fees on the same day, in an order different from their due dates.
# Post an in-advance payment dated before that day.
# Observe which fees it pays.

*Proposed fix:* when both operations are charges with equal effective and submitted dates, compare their due dates (nulls last) before falling back to creation time. Add a unit test with charges created out of due-date order.

summary: Send Asynchronous Events job sends at most one batch per run: default ceiling is 1000 events per minute
description:
Measured on current develop (4684c66), PostgreSQL, Kafka producer enabled. SavingsDepositBusinessEvent enabled, with a backlog of 12,488 TO_BE_SENT events.

 

Defaults (job "Send Asynchronous Events" with cron 0 0/1 * * * ?, external-event-batch-size = 1000): exactly 1000 events were sent per run, one run per minute, i.e. about 17 events/s or 1.4M events/day. A run takes only 0.12-0.28 s. With external-event-batch-size = 10000 the remaining 7,488 events were sent in a single run in 1.08 s (about 6,900 events/s).

 

So the ceiling comes from the configuration, not from processing cost: SendAsynchronousEventsTasklet reads one batch per execution and returns RepeatStatus.FINISHED. Operators have to know to raise the batch size or the schedule.

 

Proposal: add fineract.events.external.max-batches-per-run (default 1, so the current behavior is unchanged). A run reads up to that many batches, marks each batch as sent before reading the next one, and stops as soon as a batch is not full. A failed send leaves the failed batch TO_BE_SENT and stops the run, as today.

 

Question for maintainers: is the one-batch-per-run behavior intentional (for example to bound the run time per scheduler slot)? If not, should the default be raised later?

 

I have a branch with the change and unit tests, and a benchmark harness (docker compose override plus a k6 script). I will open a pull request once this ticket exists, and I will add before/after numbers measured on a build of the change.
